item.title: Fountain of Life crisis: Jimmy Odukoya alleges conspiracy
item.description: By Ebunoluwa Sessou The leadership crisis rocking The Fountain of Life Church has taken a fresh turn, with its Senior Pastor, Pastor Jimmy Odukoya, breaking his silence on allegations surrounding his leadership, the controversial succession video involving his late father and claims of financial impropriety. Addressing church workers on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, Odukoya gave his account of the prolonged disagreements between him, members of the church’s Board of Trustees (BOT) and his sisters, insisting that he remains the Senior Pastor despite the controversy. The meeting, which reportedly attracted about 300 workers, provided an opportunity for the embattled cleric to explain his position following the circulation of a video in which his late father, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, allegedly indicated a succession preference involving Pastor Kunle Areogun. Odukoya, who arrived at the church premises in a convoy of about five vehicles accompanied by security personnel, entered the auditorium at about 6.45 p.m. and was received with applause by the workers. Speaking emotionally, he said he had endured considerable distress over the crisis but initially chose to remain silent in the hope that the disagreements would be resolved internally. He said the decision by some board members to make his late father’s succession video public compelled him to address the workers and clarify issues surrounding the leadership dispute. Succession video and father’s instruction One of the major issues addressed by Odukoya was the video in which his late father reportedly expressed a preference for Areogun to take over the church’s leadership after his death. He said the recording was made around 2021, shortly before his father travelled to the United States for surgery. According to him, his father, uncertain about the outcome of the medical procedure, decided to document his thoughts on the future leadership of the church. Odukoya said he personally recorded the video, while his late father’s elder brother, John Odukoya, was also aware of the exercise. He, however, admitted that he retained the recording despite his father’s subsequent instruction to delete it after the surgery was successful. “Following my father’s successful surgery, he instructed me to delete the recording because the circumstances that prompted its creation had changed, but I chose to retain the video against my father’s instruction and this I admit as a grave mistake,” he said. He added that only a few people, including his sisters, knew about the recording. The disclosure raises questions about the circumstances surrounding the recording, its intended status after the surgery and the decision to make it public several years later. It also brings into focus the distinction between a succession preference expressed by the late founder and the formal governance processes through which leadership of the church is determined. item.title: Ban sign-out ceremonies at all levels of education, say parents, student leaders
item.description: By Adesina Wahab In recent years, a fad has taken root in Nigeria’s education system, the practice of signing out of school when students conclude their examinations, even without being sure of what the results would look like. It is especially rampant at secondary school and tertiary education levels. Out of what many have labelled youthful exuberance, the graduating students do engage in various activities, including holding wild parties. Read Also: (Video) UNN Party Tragedy: How I regained consciousness, found friends lying lifeless – Survivor In May this year, many parents, guardians and even teachers were left bewildered when the social media was full of videos of some male secondary school students fondling their female counterparts in broad daylight. Some male students were also seen signing on the uniforms of their female colleagues in their private areas. The students were traced to a particular school in Ondo State and punishment meted out to them. But at tertiary education level, wild parties and binge drinking have led to unnecessary deaths. Only in April this year, after the second convocation ceremony of Bamidele Olumilua University of Education, Science and Technology (BOUESTI) in Ikere-Ekiti, Ekiti State, three persons, two of whom were graduating students of the university, died in a stampede that resulted from a fight at a party thrown by some students of the university. A member of staff of the hotel where the party was held was the third casualty. Investigations by the Police revealed that a fight broke out during the party and that sharp objects were freely used, leading to people scampering for safety and many people being trampled upon. Scores of people sustained varying degrees of injuries. Just few days ago, the news broke that some students of the University of Nigeria, Nsukka, died as a result of what they consumed at a sign-out party organised by some graduating students. The figure initially given was eight but in the end, four students were confirmed dead. Even if it was one person that died, human life is too valuable to be toyed with. Reacting to the development, the Governor of Enugu State, Peter Mbah, described the deaths as a grievous loss, not only to the immediate families of the deceased and the university, but also to Enugu State as a whole. He called for a ban on sign-out parties among undergraduates, noting that the practice had brought too much sorrow to families and tertiary institutions across the country. “I received with rude shock and deep sense of loss the news of the off-campus sing-out party leading to the death of four students of the University of Nigeria Nsukka, and hospitalisation of six others. “This is a grievous loss not only to the immediate families of the deceased and the university, but also to us as a state. item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, November 19, 2026
item.description: The Nigerian naira opened early morning trading on Thursday, November 19, 2026, with diverging trends across the official and informal currency segments, as the official interbank spot market showed mild appreciation while the parallel market maintained pressure above the ₦1,440 threshold. Official Market Performance Real-time interbank spot tracking at the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM) placed the US dollar at ₦1,350.50 as of early Thursday morning, reflecting a slight gain of 0.10 percent for the local currency from its early session opening of ₦1,351.81. This follows Wednesday’s official volume-weighted closing benchmark of ₦1,363.23 per dollar published by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN). Parallel Market Rates In the parallel market, also referred to as the black market, Bureau de Change (BDC) operators and street dealers in Lagos and Abuja quoted the US dollar within a selling band of ₦1,445 to ₦1,468, with buying rates hovering between ₦1,435 and ₦1,455 depending on transaction volume and location. Following Wednesday’s late trading close where street rates climbed as high as ₦1,453 to ₦1,468, the spread between the official NFEM benchmark and the informal market stands between ₦90 and ₦105 per dollar. Market Drivers and Reserve Outlook Currency analysts attribute the persistent divergence between both windows to moderating autonomous foreign exchange inflows alongside heightened seasonal import demand and corporate obligations. Market data indicates that weekly inflows into the foreign exchange market recently moderated to $807.6 million as offshore portfolio investors adopted a cautious stance. Despite recent liquidity interventions by the apex bank—which have trimmed Nigeria’s external reserves by approximately $390 million from their late-October peak of $55.26 billion—the country’s reserve buffer remains over 26 percent higher than the $43.54 billion recorded during the corresponding period in 2025. Financial institutions expect the Central Bank of Nigeria to sustain targeted liquidity support to keep official NFEM rates anchored within the ₦1,350 to ₦1,365 band, even as unfulfilled retail demand continues to drive premiums in the parallel segment. item.title: American strategist denies receiving $4.5m for Tinubu interview
item.description: By Nwafor Sunday Polycarp, Online News Editor American political strategist and media personality, Diana London, has denied receiving $4.5 million from the Nigerian government for her recent interview with President Bola Tinubu. London, in a post on her X account on Wednesday night, described the allegation as a smear campaign, insisting that neither the Nigerian government nor anyone else in the country paid her the reported sum. She said her visit to Nigeria was to interview Tinubu for a documentary and to see the country for herself. “I unequivocally deny the claim that Nigeria’s government nor anyone else in Nigeria paid me $4.5 million. I went to Nigeria to interview President Tinubu @officialABAT for parts of a documentary and see Nigeria for myself. “This SMEAR CAMPAIGN can make noise, but can’t change the facts or stop me from speaking the truth,” she wrote. The denial comes amid controversy surrounding her interview with Tinubu at the Presidential Villa, Abuja, on Tuesday, and reports alleging that she was linked to a $4.5 million lobbying arrangement involving the Nigerian government in the United States. Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar had called on the Presidency to clarify whether the interview was connected to the reported lobbying contract and disclose the details of the arrangement. In a statement issued on Wednesday by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku said US filings identified London as a consultant to DCI Group AZ, a firm reportedly engaged by the Nigerian government through Aster Legal. He said the filings indicated that DCI Group received a $4.5 million retainer but maintained that the Presidency should clarify whether the interview formed part of the contract. Atiku demanded the publication of the contract, details of the payment and the release of the full, unedited recording of the interview. He also questioned the nature of the engagement, arguing that the Presidency should establish whether the encounter was an independent journalistic exercise or part of a government-funded publicity arrangement. The former vice president further asked the government to disclose who authorised the payment, the source of the funds and whether public money was involved. The controversy followed London’s earlier social media posts praising the security partnership between Nigeria and the United States under Tinubu and US President Donald Trump. In one of the posts, she described Nigeria as the United States’ greatest ally in Africa, saying the security cooperation between both countries was producing results and could create further economic and trade opportunities. She also expressed appreciation for the opportunity to work with individuals representing Nigeria in efforts to strengthen relations between the Trump administration and the Nigerian government. item.title: South-South: Incumbents, heavyweights in make or mar gov battles
item.description: By Jimitota Onoyume WITH the 2027 general elections approaching, the battle for four governorship seats across the South-South is gathering momentum, with incumbents, political heavyweights and emerging contenders positioning themselves for control of the region’s political landscape. In Akwa Ibom, Governor Umo Eno is banking on his performance, incumbency and the mass defection of Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, members to the All Progressives Congress, APC, to secure a second term. In Cross River, Governor Bassey Otu enjoys the advantages of incumbency, federal backing and expanding political alliances, but faces a determined challenge from PDP’s Arthur Jarvis Archibong. Rivers presents a more complicated contest, with the influence of FCT Minister Nyesom Wike, the political grievances arising from the protracted power struggle in the state and the growing appeal of opposition parties shaping the calculations. In Delta, Governor Sheriff Oborevwori appears to enjoy an advantageous position following his defection to the APC and the support of influential political leaders, while opposition candidates seek to exploit the changing political alignments. Across the four states, the contests will test the strength of incumbency, party structures, political alliances, grassroots mobilisation and the capacity of opposition candidates to convert public support into electoral victories. There will be no governorship polls in Bayelsa and Edo. Eno holds ace as opposition plots upset in Akwa Ibom Governor Umo Eno of the APC appears to have the upper hand in the battle for Akwa Ibom Government House, facing former senator and minister, John Akpanudoedehe of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, and former House of Representatives member, Michael Enyong of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC. Eno, who hails from Akwa Ibom North-East Senatorial District, Uyo, enjoys the advantage of incumbency and the political boost arising from the defection of several PDP members to the APC. His performance in office over the last three and a half years is also being projected as a major selling point as he seeks another four years. Although Akpanudoedehe commands considerable political recognition in the state, and Enyong brings legislative experience to the contest, observers believe the incumbent’s political machinery and expanding support base could prove difficult to dislodge. A public affairs analyst, Mr Ben Ikoriko, believes Eno’s empowerment programmes, particularly for people at the lower end of the state’s economy, could secure him substantial electoral support. He said: “Umo Eno will win. Yes, there are two other contenders; Akpanudoedehe and Enyong, the governor has done well and deserves a second term. Again, the PDP crossed to the APC. item.title: Tompolo’s N3.6bn fleet raises questions
item.description: The Chief Executive Officer of Tantita Security Services Nigeria Limited, which safeguards some of the nation’s critical oil and gas assets, Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, has donated over 600 vehicles estimated at about N3.68 billion to support the re-election campaign of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu across states. Tompolo, a former militant leader, doubles as the Grand Patron of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement, a group mobilising support for Tinubu’s re-election. Daily Trust reports that the cost of the vehicles has exceeded the N500 million individual donation limit under the Electoral Act 2026, but the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) says the question of whether non-cash donations are covered by the law may require judicial interpretation. The vehicles constitute a series of donations committed to supporting President Tinubu and other All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates ahead of the 2027 general elections. Gov Sani flags off five roads in Kaduna communities Adebutu’s return to ballot signals APC’s defeat in Ogun – PDP scribe There have also been pledges, including a promise of N10 million reward to each ward councilor in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) by the FCT Minister, Nyesom Wike. The proposed reward would amount to N620 million if all 62 councillors deliver their respective wards. The material donations have renewed concerns among observers over compliance with the provisions of the Electoral Act on campaign spending limits. Section 92(8) of the act provides that an individual or other entity shall not donate more than N500 million to a candidate. Under subsection (9), a candidate who knowingly contravenes the provision is liable, upon conviction, to a fine of one per cent of the permitted campaign expenditure limit, imprisonment for up to 12 months, or both. An individual who knowingly exceeds the donation limit is liable to a fine of five times the excess amount under subsection (10). Although there is no public evidence to show that Tompolo has donated sums above the N500m threshold to the Tinubu campaign, media reports revealed that he has so far distributed about 633 vehicles across at least 21 states through PBAT Door-to-Door Movement. The vehicles comprise 583 Opel Zafira wagons and 50 Sharon, with a combined market value estimated at N3.68 billion, based on average prices of fairly used vehicles of the respective models. The donations have raised questions about compliance with the electoral law and attempts by individuals to circumvent it by opting for non-cash donations. item.title: Govt of the day serving interests of few – Ndume
item.description: By Dickson Omobola Senator representing Borno South Senatorial District, Ali Ndume, Wednesday, admitted being part of the country’s political failure, saying government of the day is a government of some people, by some people and for some people. Ndume also lamented rising political violence in the country, saying anyone found sponsoring such acts should be held responsible. Speaking on Prime Time, an Arise Television programme, he expressed dissatisfaction with the manner in which public office holders were amassing wealth, saying many of them were gluttons. He said: “I am part of the failure, I cannot deny that. I am not going to claim to be the best or better than anybody. But if I had known that this is how this politics is going to turn out to be, I wouldn’t have joined it. You can compare politics to AIDS. Once you catch it, you can’t say you don’t have AIDS. I’m telling you. It’s a dangerous game, especially in Nigeria. You can’t get cured. “It’s true that government of the day has been a government of some people, by some people and for some people. If it were a government of all, this complaint and all that would not be happening. It did not start with this government. It started with the previous government. It has become a practice that you must be within the cycle. Even within the cycle, there are cabals running the government.” On violence as a tool for political competition, he said: “In fact, that is why I am happy that everybody is concerned, so that we may nip it in the bud. My friend and colleague, Ningi, moved the motion after we spoke, and I seconded the motion. Then you can see how our colleagues showed concern, and Nigerians generally. It is one of the motions that was apolitical because the problem is like fire. If it catches, you don’t know when it will stop, and you may have a problem putting it off. “It has also happened in a few countries where things got out of hand and, in extreme cases, reached a stage where the country’s government collapsed. You could see what happened in Bangladesh. Some years back, you could hear what happened in the Middle East. “When people easily take the law into their own hands to express their hunger and use whatever is available that can be regarded as a weapon or tool, then it becomes a dangerous thing.” Vanguard News The post Govt of the day serving interests of few – Ndume appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Anchor Borrowers Scheme: Reps divided over calls to write off farmers’ N1trn loans waiver
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina Abuja — A motion seeking the cancellation of outstanding loans obtained by farmers under various government-backed agricultural intervention programmes yesterday divided members of the House of Representatives. Lawmakers disagreed over whether distressed farmers should be granted debt relief or subjected to an investigation. The motion, sponsored by Inuwa Garba, representing Yamaltu/Deba federal constituency of Gombe State, was predicated on the economic difficulties confronting farmers, particularly the impact of insecurity, climate change, natural disasters and other challenges that had disrupted agricultural production across the country. The federal government had, in recent years, introduced several agricultural financing initiatives, including the Anchor Borrowers’ Programme, Commercial Agriculture Credit Scheme and NIRSAL-supported facilities, to boost food production, empower farmers and strengthen national food security. Leading debate on the motion, Garba said insecurity, banditry, insurgency, farmer-herder clashes, flooding, drought and other environmental challenges had significantly undermined agricultural activities, resulting in crop failures, loss of investments and reduced farm incomes. He argued that many beneficiaries of government-sponsored agricultural loans were unable to meet their repayment obligations, not because they were unwilling to repay, but because circumstances beyond their control had severely affected their productive capacity and financial stability. According to him, continued accumulation and enforcement of outstanding debts, including principal, interest and penalties, can push already struggling farmers further into poverty, expose them to asset seizures and discourage participation in future agricultural activities. However, opposing the proposed debt cancellation, Bamidele Salam, representing Ede South/Ede North/Ejigbo/Egbedore federal constituency of Osun State, questioned the justification for a blanket waiver, citing findings in the Auditor-General for the Federation’s report before the House. Salam, who chairs the House Committee on Public Accounts, alleged that some beneficiaries of agricultural intervention loans running into over N1tn diverted the funds to businesses and personal investments. unrelated to farming. He said some beneficiaries who approached the Central Bank of Nigeria and commercial banks for agricultural loans allegedly channelled the funds into real estate acquisitions in Abuja, Lagos and even Dubai. He also expressed concern over the state of the Bank of Agriculture which, he said, had been rendered virtually immobile by N795billion in loans owed by beneficiaries, many of whom allegedly diverted the funds. Salam warned that approving a blanket waiver without establishing how the loans were utilised would set a dangerous precedent for future government intervention programmes. item.title: FAAC disburses N2.4trn to FG, states, LGs in October
item.description: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief ABUJA — THE Federation Account Allocation Committee, FAAC, yesterday, shared the sum of N2.441 trillion among the three tiers of government. The amount was from the October 2026 Federation Account Revenue, which was shared at the FAAC meeting held in Abuja on Wednesday. The N2.441 trillion comprised distributable statutory revenue of N1.688 trillion and Value Added Tax (VAT) revenue of N752.488 billion. A communiqué issued by the Federation Account Allocation Committee, FAAC, indicated that gross revenue of N3.811 trillion was available in the month of October 2026. Total deduction for cost of collection was N128.797 billion while total transfers, refunds and savings stood at N1.241 trillion. According to the communiqué sent by Director of Press of the Office of the Accountant-General of the Federation, Bawa Mokwa, gross statutory revenue of N2.999 trillion was received for the month of October 2026. This was lower than the sum of N3.096 trillion received in the preceding month by N97.323 billion. Gross revenue of N812.446 billion was available from the Value Added Tax (VAT) in October 2026. This was lower than the N816.872 billion available in the month of September 2026 by N4.426 billion. The communiqué stated that from the N2.441 trillion total distributable revenue, the Federal Government received a total sum of N856.065 billion and the state governments received a total sum of N809.909 billion. The Local Government Councils received N568.701 billion, while the sum of N206.384 billion (13% of mineral revenue) was shared to the benefiting State as derivation revenue. On the N1.688 trillion distributable statutory revenue, the Federal Government received N780.816 billion and the State Governments received N396.040 billion. The Local Government Councils received N305.331 billion and the sum of N206.384 billion (13% of mineral revenue) was shared to the benefiting States as derivation revenue. From the N752.488 billion distributable Value Added Tax (VAT) revenue, the Federal Government received N75.249 billion, the State Governments received N413.868 billion and the Local Government Councils received N263.371 billion. In October 2026, Excise Duty and CET Levies increased marginally, while Petroleum Profit Tax (PPT), Hydrocarbon Tax (HT), Petroleum Royalties, Import Duty, Companies Income Tax (CIT), CGT & SDT, Value Added Tax (VTA), Mineral Royalties, and Gas Flared Penalty, Rental Gas Flared Fee and Misc. Oil Revenue all decreased. Vanguard News The post FAAC disburses N2.4trn to FG, states, LGs in October appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: State police on verge of reality; operational guidelines bill submitted to Justice Ministry
item.description: By Henry Umoru & Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — Operation of State police in Nigeria is at the verge of being realised. The National Assembly yesterday transmitted the bill ratified by the 36 state houses of Assembly to President Bola Tinubu yesterday for assent. The lawmakers asked the president to send a bill on the operational guidelines for state police for passage. Chief of Staff to president, Femi Gbajabiamila disclosed yesterday that the operational guidelines bill has been forwarded to the Ministry of Justice for validation. To quicken the process, the Senate asked President Tinubu to forward to the National Assembly the National Policing Bill which would provide for the operationlisation of state police across the 36 states of the federation for legislative scrutiny and expeditious passage. It also mandated the clerk to the National Assembly, CNA, Kamoru Ogunlana to transmit the constitutional amendment bill that seeks to establish State Police Services in Nigeria to the President for assent, having satisfied all the constitutional requirements, in line with the Acts Authentication Act, 2004. President Tinubu, however, received the State Police Bill later yesterday, with the Chief of Staff to the President, Mr, Femi Gbajabiamila, saying the bill requested by the Senate had been submitted to the Federal Ministry of Justice for legislative drafting validation. According to him, upon receipt of the validated version, the President Working Group, which he chairs, will review and present it, alongside its report to the President for consideration. Resolutions of the Senate were sequel to a motion, titled “Passage of Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026 and sponsored by the Senate Leader, Senator Opeyemi Bamidele. Bamidele, who urged the President to forward to the Senate expeditiously the National Policing Bill, said in his presentation: “The Senate: Recall that pursuant to Section 9(1) of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999, the National Assembly processed an Executive Bill seeking to alter the provisions of the Constitution to establish State Police as part of the national policing structure. “Also recall that the Senate and the House of Representatives on June 24 and July, 23, 2026, respectively, overwhelmingly supported the bill with over 2/3 majority votes, thereby meeting the constitutional threshold for the passage of the bill by the National Assembly; “Aware that the National Assembly transmitted the bill to the 36 State Houses of Assembly for the mandatory approval by resolution of not less than 2/3 majority of the State Houses of Assembly as provided by Section 9(2) of the Constitution before the Bill can be passed; The states… “Also aware that the 36 State Houses of Assembly have transmitted their resolution of the bill to the National Assembly, namely Abia, Adamawa, Anambra, Akwa-Ibom, Bauchi, Bayelsa, Benue, Borno, Cross-River, Delta, Ebonyi, Edo, Ekiti, Enugu, Gombe, Im

item.title: US Democrats nominate Jeffries to be first Black House speaker
item.description: Hakeem Jeffries is on the cusp of becoming the first Black speaker of the US House of Representatives after Democrats elected him their leader Wednesday following a sweeping midterm election triumph. The 56-year-old New Yorker secured 251 votes in a closed-door, secret ballot, with 11 cast against his nomination, according to US media. Jeffries faced no declared challenger, although opposition from some newly elected progressives had exposed divisions over how Democrats should wield their newfound power. His nomination puts him on course to preside over a commanding Democratic majority during the final two years of President Donald Trump’s term, as his party prepares to reverse Republican policies and investigate the administration. Jeffries must still win a formal vote of the full House when the new Congress convenes on January 3, when he would become the first Black politician to hold the powerful post. With a large Democratic majority, this is seen as something of a formality. Both returning Democrats and incoming lawmakers participated in Wednesday’s election, including progressives who had sought concessions on issues ranging from US military support for Israel to the influence of money in politics. Jeffries had requested a recorded vote rather than a nomination “by acclamation” — without a formal ballot — as some allies had hoped. He argued that every Democrat should have an opportunity to weigh his experience, record and vision, citing the precedent set when the party last took control of the House in 2018. The ballot remained secret, with the overall tally made public but individual votes kept anonymous. Ahead of the election, Jeffries met progressive lawmakers to discuss issues including Israel and healthcare, with proposals to lower the Medicare eligibility age and expand coverage among the topics discussed. The Democratic leader has also sought to shift attention to the party’s plans for governing after voters handed Republicans a crushing defeat amid anger over the Iran war and soaring fuel costs. “Folks are drowning in this Republican economy, and House Democrats are committed to turning that situation around, beginning on day one,” he told reporters Tuesday. “We’re going to relentlessly fight for an affordable America.” – Brooklyn roots – Raised in Brooklyn’s working-class Crown Heights neighborhood, Jeffries trained as a lawyer before entering the New York state legislature in 2007 and winning election to Congress in 2012. Known for his measured manner, sharp rhetoric and penchant for quoting hip-hop artists, he became the first Black politician to lead a party in either chamber of Congress when Democrats chose him to succeed Nancy Pelosi in 2022. He also served as a House prosecutor during Trump’s first impeachment trial in 2020. As speaker, Jeffries would preside over one of Washington’s most powerful institutions and stand second in line to the presidency behind the vice president. item.title: FIFA picks Amokachi, four others to oversee NFF until May 2027
item.description: World football governing body FIFA has appointed former Super Eagles striker Daniel Amokachi and four others to a five-member normalisation committee tasked with overseeing the affairs of the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF). The committee will be chaired by former NFF electoral committee chairman Sampson Ebomhe and is expected to manage the federation’s transition and organise fresh elections for a new leadership. Its mandate will run until May 31, 2027, at the latest. FIFA communicated the appointments in a letter sent to the NFF secretariat on Wednesday, following consultations with the Confederation of African Football (CAF). Other members of the committee are governance expert Dr Joe Abah, veteran sports journalist and administrator Godwin Enakhena, and Amina Yerima. “We refer to the decision of the Bureau of the FIFA Council of 22 October 2026 to appoint a normalisation committee for the Nigeria Football Federation. “In this respect, following consultation with CAF, we hereby communicate the composition of the normalisation committee as follows: Mr Sampson Ebomhe (chairman), Dr Joe Abah (member), Mr Godwin Enakhena (member), Ms Amina Yerima (member) and Mr Daniel Amokachi (member),” the letter read. The world football governing body said the appointees would commence their duties immediately, subject to eligibility screening by its Review Committee in line with FIFA Governance Regulations. Their final confirmation will depend on the outcome of the screening exercise. FIFA also prohibited members of the committee from contesting any position in the forthcoming NFF elections, regardless of whether they resign or have their appointments revoked. “None of the members of the normalisation committee will be eligible for the positions to be filled during the upcoming NFF elections under any circumstances, including in the event that their mandate as a member of the normalisation committee is revoked or that they resign from their position,” the letter added. FIFA further stated that it could, in consultation with CAF, withdraw the appointment of any committee member or expand the committee by appointing additional members. The intervention follows the resignation of NFF President Ibrahim Gusau, General Secretary Mohammed Sanusi and members of the federation’s executive committee on August 27, 2026, amid growing criticism of the country’s football administration. The development disrupted arrangements for the NFF elective congress scheduled for September 27, prompting FIFA and CAF to step in and approve the establishment of a normalisation committee to supervise the transition. Ebomhe, who will lead the committee, has previously held several positions in Nigerian sports administration. In August 2025, he was appointed vice-chairman of the seven-member electoral committee established by the National Sports Commission to conduct elections into national sports federations. item.title: 1966, civil war and beyond: Gowon’s unpleasant echoes of the past! By Olu Fasan
item.description: This is the last of my three-part commentary on General Yakubu Gowon’s memoirs, My Life of Duty & Allegiance. My focus this week is on the most challenging parts of the memoirs, namely, the 1966 coups, the civil war, Gowon’s overthrow as head of state, and his treatment following allegations of complicity in the abortive coup that led to the overthrow and death of then head of state General Murtala Muhammed. General Gowon’s accounts of these events reflect very unpleasant echoes of the past. Although he says that “by choosing to write, I made a conscious decision not to reopen old wounds”, he does exactly that, with unsavoury views, particularly on Emeka Ojukwu, Murtala Muhammed and Olusegun Obasanjo. Unsurprisingly, several Igbo commentators have strongly condemned Gowon’s accounts of the civil war, with some calling him a “liar”. But those Igbos must admit that it’s such a shame Ojukwu died without writing his own memoirs. As it is, the last words on the 1966 coups, the civil war and its aftermath are those of Gowon, who was Army Chief of Staff during the 1966 events, and head of state during the civil war. With Ojukwu not alive to rebut Gowon, and not having left behind his memoirs, it’s hard for anyone to dismiss Gowon’s assessment of Ojukwu out of hand. And Gowon’s assessment is unsparing! Truth be told, the civil war was a war of conflicting egos, fuelled by a deep rivalry between two proud leaders: Gowon and Ojukwu. Under different leaders, the war, perhaps, would not have happened. But Ojukwu loathed Gowon and refused to recognise his leadership, insisting he was his senior in the army hierarchy. On his part, Gowon viewed Ojukwu as a politically ambitious and disloyal officer who always had coup motives. Indeed, according to Gowon, the precursor to the January 15, 1966 coup was Ojukwu’s earlier plan in 1964 to intervene militarily in favour of Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe, the titular president, in the dispute between him and Sir Tafawa Balewa, the prime minister, over the controversial 1964 general elections. Gowon also cites a report that “suggested Ojukwu knew about the (January 15, 1966) coup and might have been involved in it.” The absence of friendship or mutual respect, let alone trust, between them thwarted well-meaning efforts to prevent the war! Interestingly, both parties somewhat used Chief Obafemi Awolowo’s statement to justify fighting the war. In May 1967, two months before the war began, Chief Awolowo told a meeting of the Western Leaders of Thought in Ibadan: “If the Eastern Region is allowed by acts of omission or commission to secede from or opt out of Nigeria, then the Western Region and Lagos must also stay out of the Federation.” Today, some Igbos still argue that, with that statement, Awolowo misled Ojukwu into declaring secession, ignoring the statement’s key proviso. But for Gowon, Chief Awolowo’s remark gave him the resolve to stop the attempted secession. “At the back of my mind,” Gowon writes, “I remembered Chief Awolowo’

item.title: Unilorin student seeks N43m for kidney transplant
item.description: … Family spends over N20m, sells property to sustain treatment By Chioma Obinna The family of Olajide Victor, a 200-level student of the University of Ilorin, Kwara State, has appealed for N43 million to fund a kidney transplant for him after he was diagnosed with Stage V end-stage renal disease. Victor is expected to undergo the life-saving procedure at Newhaven Specialist Hospital, Lagos, as his family struggles to meet the cost of his treatment. He said his health challenges began in November 2025 after he sustained a minor fracture in his left leg while playing football at the university’s sports complex. Weeks later, his face and legs became swollen, prompting medical examinations. Following several tests, including kidney function investigations, he was diagnosed with Stage V kidney disease at Taiwo Hospital, Ilorin. A medical report signed by Dr S. Alagbe, Consultant Nephrologist, indicated that Victor requires continued haemodialysis twice weekly. His mother, Comfort Adesanya, said the family had spent over N20 million on his treatment and sold their land, house and other valuables to keep him alive. She appealed to individuals, corporate organisations and well-meaning Nigerians to help raise the N43 million required for the transplant, saying the family could no longer cope with the rising cost of treatment. Donations can be made to Victor Adekunle Olajide, UBA, Account Number: 2458216260 or call Victor on 09018866426. The post Unilorin student seeks N43m for kidney transplant appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Labour leaders, politicians, sympathiers shut Abia for fallen NLC scribe
item.description: *As Ajaero, Otti, others bid farewell to Ugboaja By Victor Ahiuma-Young & Steve Oko From a solemn evening of solidarity in the United States, to the Day of Tributes in Abuja, and from the Service of Songs in Lagos to the funeral service and interment in Abia, the consensus was the same: Emmanuel Okechukwu Ugboaja, the late General-Secretary of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC), was a rare breed of labour leader whose influence transcended the workplace. He moved in the corridors of power, interacted with presidents and influential political figures, and served on national and international platforms, yet his heart remained firmly with ordinary Nigerian workers and the downtrodden. For Ugboaja, power was never an excuse to abandon the masses, while influence was meaningful only when deployed in the service of humanity. That philosophy defined his more than three decades in the labour movement and earned him a reputation as a fearless defender of workers’ rights. But on Saturday, November 14, the voice that once spoke boldly for the voiceless fell silent forever. As family members, labour leaders, government officials, political associates and sympathisers gathered in his Nkpa community, Abia State, to bid him a final farewell, tears mingled with tributes to a man whom NLC President, Comrade Joe Ajaero, described as more than a friend and brother, but someone in whom he found a part of himself. At 60, Ugboaja’s death ended a remarkable journey, but the tributes at his burial underscored a legacy of courage, loyalty, selflessness and unwavering commitment to social justice. Emotional farewell For Ajaero, losing Ugboaja went beyond the death of a fellow labour leader. It was the loss of a trusted confidant, comrade-in-arms and a man with whom he shared nearly three decades of friendship, professional engagement and ideological struggles. Speaking in an emotional tribute at the burial, the NLC president admitted that he might not be the best person to speak about the deceased because of the depth of their relationship. “Ugboaja was not just a friend. I don’t know how else to describe him. He was more than a brother. We shared the same fate. We are brothers in Christ and comrades in this family. We shared secrets. I found in him part of me,” Ajaero said. His words offered a glimpse into a relationship that transcended organised labour, becoming a deep personal bond built on trust, shared experiences and common convictions. Ajaero described his late friend as a perfect gentleman, dependable, courageous and one of the finest personalities in the labour movement Perhaps the most striking aspect of Ugboaja’s character, according to him, was his ability to maintain relationships with the powerful without compromising his loyalty to ordinary Nigerians. He recalled that the late labour leader knew influential personalities, including successive presidents and members of presidential committees, yet remained committed to defending the interests of the masses.

item.title: Senate’s latest summons of telcos
item.description: The Senate’s latest intervention over Nigeria’s troubled telecommunications services is welcome, but Nigerians have heard this music before. On 11th November, 2026, lawmakers directed their Communications Committee, chaired by Senator Aliyu Ikra Bilbis, to engage the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) and operators MTN, Airtel, Globacom and T2 over dropped calls, failed connections, interrupted conversations and deductions for unauthorised subscriptions. The motion was sponsored by Senate Chief Whip Tahir Monguno, presented by Deputy Majority Leader Lola Ashiru and supported by Ned Nwoko. The committee has four weeks to establish subscribers’ losses and recommend action. Senate President Godswill Akpabio warned that unsatisfactory explanations could trigger a Committee of the Whole and summonses to the Minister, Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) leadership and operators. The complaints are familiar. Calls fail to connect, terminate abruptly or become inaudible, yet airtime is deducted. Customers redial and pay again. Subscribers also complain of data bundles disappearing rapidly, unexplained balance depletion, unsolicited “value-added” subscriptions and caller tunes activated and billed without consent, as well as charges they cannot trace. Streaming, background applications and automatic updates can legitimately consume data; that makes itemised usage records essential. The Senate must distinguish genuine network-related losses from legitimate consumption and unauthorised billing. This is hardly the first legislative alarm. The Senate acted on dropped calls and deductions in 2017 and 2019. The House adopted a similar resolution in December 2023 over poor voice quality, wrong-number connections and zero-voice charges. In October 2026, a House ad hoc committee summoned operators’ chief executives over deteriorating services. After operators failed to appear and their industry association sought to represent them, the committee renewed its demand and warned of possible arrest warrants. The present inquiry is at least the fifth major parliamentary intervention in this recurring dispute. The NCC is no spectator. Under the Nigerian Communications Act, it licenses and regulates operators, sets service standards, monitors performance, protects consumers and imposes sanctions. It has quality benchmarks and an automatic airtime compensation framework for qualifying service failures. Yet complaints persist. The regulator must explain its enforcement, refunds and compensation record, not merely recite regulations. This time, lawmakers must publish hearing evidence, demand independent audits of call-detail and billing records, require chief executives to attend, set deadlines for refunds and measurable improvements, and report publicly on compliance. item.title: Food security: Nigerian farmers risk wasting billions on fertilisers without soil testing, experts warn
item.description: By Adeola Badru & Cynthia Alo Nigeria’s quest for food security may continue to suffer setbacks unless farmers move away from indiscriminate fertiliser application and embrace soil testing and crop-specific nutrient management, agricultural experts have warned. The experts, who spoke at the 2026 South-West Nigeria Fertiliser and Soil Health Summit in Ibadan, Oyo State, cautioned that increasing fertiliser consumption without understanding the specific nutrient requirements of farmland could undermine agricultural productivity, weaken farmers’ incomes and worsen soil degradation. They argued that the country’s approach to fertiliser management must go beyond distributing inputs to farmers and focus on ensuring that the right fertiliser is applied to the right soil, for the right crop and at the appropriate time. The position formed a major highlight of the communiqué issued at the end of the summit, organised by the Institute of Agricultural Research and Training (IAR&T), Obafemi Awolowo University, Moor Plantation, Ibadan, on Tuesday. With the theme, “Fertilisers and Food Security in South-West Nigeria: The Journey So Far,” the summit brought together more than 150 scientists, farmers, policymakers, fertiliser manufacturers and distributors, agricultural extension professionals and development partners to examine the challenges confronting fertiliser utilisation and soil health in the region. The participants expressed concern that the continued reliance on blanket fertiliser recommendations failed to address significant differences in soil fertility, acidity, phosphorus fixation, nutrient depletion and other soil-related challenges across different agroecological zones. According to the communiqué, “The predominance of blanket fertiliser recommendations does not adequately address the variations in soil fertility, soil acidity, phosphorus fixation, nutrient depletion and other soil constraints across different agroecological zones in the region.” The experts maintained that fertiliser recommendations should increasingly be based on soil testing, crop requirements, prevailing agroecological conditions and economically viable nutrient management practices. They also identified high fertiliser prices, inadequate distribution networks, limited access to credit and inconsistent availability as major constraints preventing smallholder farmers from accessing and effectively utilising the agricultural input. The summit further warned that declining soil organic matter, nutrient imbalance, erosion and other forms of soil degradation continued to undermine fertiliser-use efficiency and agricultural productivity. item.title: [VIDEO] Tinubu Can’t Alter State Police Bill, He’ll Definitely Sign It — Omole
item.description: Lawyer and author Charles Omole has said that he does not expect President Bola Tinubu to make an alteration to the National Policing Bill transmitted to him by the National Assembly. Omole, who stated this during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Wednesday. He explained that altering the bill would return the process to the Senate, House of Representatives and state houses of assembly for their approval. Omole noted further that the constitutional amendment is not the meat and bone of policing but simply allows state police to exist, while the National Policing Bill specifies the structure and functions of the state police. He, however, said that the National Policing Bill could not be considered until the constitutional amendment had gone through. He explained that while the 36 states would have their own police service, the police in the Federal Capital Territory would be under the control of the federal police service. Omole, however, said that part of the recommendation under the bill is that states cannot buy their own arms and ammunition at will. item.title: Plateau 2027: PDP’s Scores Gov Mutfwang 15-20% In Performance
item.description: The governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Kephas Ropshik, on Wednesday said that Governor Caleb Mutfwang performed poorly in governance in the state. Ropshik, who spoke during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today , said the governor had not scored more than 20 per cent in performance. The PDP candidate said that leadership should be about performance and about the people. “In fact, I can tell you on a scale of one to 100, you can give him like 15 to 20 per cent in performance,” he said. “He still remains someone that I respect, but of course that, completely, is different from politics.” ﻿ He alleged that the governor defected to the All Progressives Congress (APC) when he could not cope with the crisis in the PDP. He, however, said that the governor did not leave with up to 15 per cent of the members of the PDP, insisting that Plateau is a PDP state. “You know, a man’s strength and leadership qualities are being tested when there are crises, but the governor couldn’t stand the crisis. He left for APC, and so there was an opening in the PDP to contest for governorship because, of course, the truth is this. Plateau has been a PDP state. “You can’t take that away from Plateau State, right? And so there was a vacancy, and so somebody needed to fill in the gap. And so even with the crisis, we believed in the PDP,” the candidate said. “Mutfwang did not live with 15, 20 per cent of people, I mean, in PDP to APC. The people, in fact, not even 10 per cent, because the people that followed him to APC are his appointees, and that’s the truth. “Ninety per cent of people on the Plateau still believe in the PDP.” Ropshik said that Plateau is one of the frontrunners in the Rainbow Coalition. He also said that he was working for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu. Asked whether he was not confusing his followers by telling them to vote for the APC in the January 16 presidential election, and the PDP in the February 6, 2027 governorship election in the state, Ropshik said, “No, no, no, I am not reading because now if we want to be sincere to ourselves, the PDP presidential candidate, we all know that there’s no chance for him to win the election. “And so why should we now waste the votes? We must find a platform to identify; what we’re after is good governance.” The post Plateau 2027: PDP’s Scores Gov Mutfwang 15-20% In Performance appeared first on Channels Television .
